subject: english
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution:
The correct answer is "have been."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"have been"** is used in the blank to convey the sense of a continuous or ongoing action.
 
• In this context,** "have been"** indicates that the process of being brought up to fear insects started in the past and has continued up to the present.
 
• It emphasizes the duration or continuity of the upbringing in relation to the fear of insects.
 
• 
 
Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

 
 
• 
 
**Correct paragraph**:

 

We **have been**__ brought up to fear insects. We regard them as unnecessary creatures that do more harm than good. Man continually ______ (2) ______ war on them, because they contaminate his food, carry diseases, or devour his crops. They sting or bite without provocation; they fly uninvited into our rooms on summer nights or beat against our lighted windows. We live in dread not only of unpleasant insects like spiders or wasps but of quite ______ (3) ______ ones like moths. Reading about them increases our understanding without dispelling our fears.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Let us explore other options:
 
 
• **Were being: **Using **"were being"** in the blank of the sentence would change the meaning and the tone. It would imply a passive voice construction, suggesting that someone else or some external force was involved in the process of bringing someone up to fear insects. 
 
• **Are been: **The phrase **"are been"** is not grammatically correct in standard English.
 
• **Will be being: **While **"will be being"** is grammatically correct, it is often considered awkward and can be avoided for the sake of clarity and simplicity in English. This maintains the future tense and conveys the idea without the slightly cumbersome **"will be being." **
